title: CWG 2026: Dilip Gavit wins Gold, Mohd Basil claims Silver in Men's T47 100m race
content: Dilip Gavit secured gold in the men's T47 100m race with a new Games Record. Mohammed Basil Morssinganakth followed closely, earning the silver medal for India. This remarkable performance ensured a historic one-two finish for the Indian contingent. England's Kevin Santos claimed the bronze medal in the competitive event. The athletes delivered strong performances on the track.

title: We are in India, be realistic, says HC, lifts curbs on hotel over 2 insects
content: The Bombay high court quashed a hotel's license suspension after finding minor hygiene issues.  A solitary finding of two insects did not justify the continued suspension of the license.  The court accepted the hotel's undertaking to maintain high sanitation standards.  The Food and Drug Administration's drive aims to improve food safety across Maharashtra.  The court appreciated the state and FDA actions in enforcing food safety laws.

title: Denied seat, student hacks IIT-Kanpur website to show his 'merit'
content: A BTech applicant hacked IIT Kanpur's website seeking admission consideration. He claimed he was denied a fair chance in the selection process. The IIT director invited the candidate to campus for an assessment. He stressed that hacking was not the correct approach to gain entry. The institute will consider him if genuine talent is demonstrated.

title: Murali Sreeshankar bags Silver in thrilling long jump final, misses Gold by 6 cm
content: Murali Sreeshankar secured the silver medal in the men's long jump event. He achieved a best leap of 8.09m in the fiercely contested final. Jamaica's Tajay Gayle won gold with a jump of 8.15m in the fourth round. Scotland's Stephen Mackenzie claimed the bronze medal with a jump of 8.08m. Lokesh finished fifth in his Commonwealth Games debut competition.

title: Continue with your duties fearlessly, CRPF chief tells troopers amid pellet gun row
content: CRPF Director General G P Singh supports troops acting in good faith during duty.  He assures responsibility for all decisions made in the public interest.  An internal probe found standard operating procedures were followed by RAF personnel.  Pellet guns were used after other crowd dispersal methods failed.  This investigation may prevent charges against the RAF personnel involved.

title: 'My mornings are for...': Jeff Bezos reveals he never makes any decisions before 10 am
content: Jeff Bezos prioritizes his mornings, dedicating this time to personal matters and family before diving into work. He strategically avoids challenging tasks until after 10 am, promoting a productive start to his day. He opts for critical conversations mid-morning when his mental clarity is at its peak. Research indicates that decision fatigue can hinder judgment, so Bezos emphasizes making a select number of high-quality decisions each day for maximum effectiveness.

title: 'Not going to let him get away': Rahul targets Shah over police action on NEET protesters
content: Rahul Gandhi accused Home Minister Amit Shah of police excesses against protesters.  He demanded Shah's dismissal and a Supreme Court-monitored probe into the actions.  Gandhi also blamed the RSS for the education sector's current problems.  Government ministers challenged Gandhi to provide proof or issue an apology.  The Lok Sabha experienced disruptions over these serious allegations.

title: Ahead of dengue vaccine rollout, all 4 strains found in circulation
content: India's first dengue virus mapping shows all four serotypes circulating in eight states.  This finding could influence the country's upcoming dengue vaccine strategy.  Researchers found DENV-2 to be the dominant circulating strain across the nation.  Concurrent infections with multiple strains are linked to more severe dengue disease.  Continuous molecular surveillance is essential for monitoring virus circulation and guiding policy.

title: How Europe's heatwave is proving Americans right about air conditioning
content: Europeans are now buying air conditioning units in unprecedented numbers. Manufacturers report significant sales growth across several European countries. This shift is driven by both comfort and public health concerns. Rising temperatures and extreme heat events are becoming impossible to ignore. Cultural attitudes towards cooling solutions are beginning to change.

title: Now, just one visit for NEET-UG counselling
content: NEET-UG counselling now requires only one physical reporting for candidates seeking admission. Aspirants can complete subsequent document verification online while retaining their allotted seats. The Medical Counselling Committee also introduced online resignation for surrendered seats. NRI category admissions are now fully digitized, improving verification processes. The government aims for a transparent and merit-based counselling system.

title: Barracuda bites Texas girl, 13, but cannot shake her ocean dream
content: A Texas teenager is recovering after a rare barracuda attack during a family vacation. Claire Macdonel experienced the frightening incident in shallow waters while wearing a shiny bracelet. She is now home and preparing for surgery to repair her hand injury. Despite the painful ordeal, Claire still dreams of becoming a marine biologist. Her family shares the story to raise awareness and encourage water safety precautions.

title: Oregon EMT fired after disabling ambulance cameras, files $800k lawsuit
content: A former EMT from Oregon has filed a lawsuit against her employer for $800,000, alleging wrongful termination after she disabled covert recording cameras present in ambulances. The company reportedly set up these cameras without informing patients or obtaining their consent. This case raises significant issues regarding patient privacy and the increasing trend of surveillance, particularly given the strict recording regulations in Oregon.

title: JPMorgan CEO recalls his Citigroup firing: Shares meeting with mentor Sandy Weill
content: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon discussed two major life events.  His 1998 Citigroup dismissal reshaped his career path significantly. His youngest daughter asked if the family would now have to “sleep on the streets”. A near-fatal heart emergency in 2020 brought him peace.  Dimon invested heavily in Bank One after leaving Citigroup.  This bold move led to his leadership at JPMorgan Chase.

title: Lok Sabha passes anti-paper leak bill after row over Rahul's remarks
content: The Lok Sabha passed a bill to make paper leak punishments more stringent. This legislation aims to expedite trials and deter unfair means in public examinations. The bill proposes significant jail terms and hefty fines for individuals involved in paper leaks. Investigations into paper leak cases are to be completed within two months. The government also highlighted an increase in universities and higher education institutions.

title: Rahul Gandhi remarks row: BJP hits back, calls Congress MP's claim 'a pack of lies'
content: The BJP strongly objects if Rahul Gandhi called students an idiot.  They welcome the remark if it was self-directed by the Congress leader.  BJP leaders accused Rahul Gandhi of spreading falsehoods and misleading the nation.  They stated no bullets were fired during the student protests.  The party highlighted government dialogue and efforts to strengthen laws against paper leaks.

title: No district affected by Naxalism anymore: Ministry of home affairs
content: The number of Left-wing extremism-affected districts has fallen to zero by March 2026. This marks a significant reduction from 126 districts prior to April 2018.  Maoist violence has seen a steep decline, with few incidents recorded this year.  Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand remain the only states with reported Maoist incidents.  However, 37 districts are still classified as legacy and thrust areas.

title: Lamine Yamal says his mother's sacrifices outweigh childhood struggles he endured
content: Lamine Yamal, the 19-year-old World Cup winner, has spoken openly about a childhood shaped by financial hardship and parental sacrifice. His mother, Sheila Ebana, emigrated from Equatorial Guinea to Spain as a teenager, had Yamal at 16, and raised him largely alone after separating from his father when Lamine was three. Yamal credits her with shielding him from the worst of their circumstances, saying she made him see only the beautiful side of life. He also reflected on his rapid rise at Barcelona, describing himself as a creative and entertaining player who never anticipated reaching the first team quite so quickly

title: Candace Owens shares unseen Charlie Kirk video as Alex Jones questions narrative
content: Candace Owens has released new rooftop footage that she says raises questions about whether Tyler Robinson was the person who shot Charlie Kirk. Alex Jones backed her claims, arguing the video contradicts the official case against Robinson. However, authorities still identify Robinson as the accused, and a judge has not yet ruled on whether the case will move to trial.

title: Gisele Bündchen opens up on motherhood struggles during marriage to Tom Brady
content: Tom Brady's ex wife Gisele Bündchen has gone more and more public about their lives ever since the two ended thir marriage. The Brazilian supermodel has now opened up about motherhood.

title: Amid opposition walkout, Rajya Sabha gives approval to Vande Mataram bill
content: The Rajya Sabha passed a bill proposing jail time for disrupting Vande Mataram. Opposition MPs walked out, demanding a statement on police action against protesters. Junior home minister Nityanand Rai piloted the bill, criticizing Congress's stance on the national song. MP Sanjay Singh questioned the RSS's past refusal to hoist the tricolour. AIADMK MPs noted the practice of playing state anthems after national songs.

title: Delhi high court refuses HPV shots stay, but seeks Centre's response
content: The Delhi High Court declined to halt the HPV immunisation campaign. Authorities must now explain the vaccine's introduction within four weeks. The court emphasized the need for proper protocols before administering vaccines. A Public Interest Litigation raised concerns about long-term safety and consent. The next hearing for this matter is scheduled for October 29.

title: Government: North-east cartels shifting towards synthetic drugs
content: Northeast drug syndicates are shifting towards synthetic drugs from Myanmar. They are increasingly using social media and encrypted apps for coordination. Traffickers exploit porous borders and forest routes for cross-border smuggling. Narcotics are concealed in legitimate cargo and passenger vehicles. Moreh-Tamu border remains a key transit point for these drugs.

title: Pathologist's claims raise fresh questions over Nolan Wells' final hours and death
content: Nolan Wells' death has sparked shockwaves across the nation as the cause behind it remains unknown. Amid this, a new claim has been made by a pathologist.

title: Here's why many MBBS graduates can't take foreign licensing exams
content: Thousands of MBBS graduates cannot take foreign licensing exams. Their colleges have not secured ECFMG sponsor notes for global recognition. This formal note is essential for students seeking international medical practice opportunities. Many students discover this issue only after completing their medical degrees. The National Medical Commission is processing updates for several Indian medical colleges.

title: With 90 out of 128 cos & 64% of investments, K'taka top beneficiary of Centre's EDF scheme
content: Karnataka received the most funding from the central government's Electronics Development Fund.  The fund's associated venture funds invested over Rs 1,335 crore in 128 companies.  Karnataka-based firms secured Rs 854.5 crore, representing nearly two-thirds of total investments.  Telangana, Maharashtra, and Delhi also saw significant investments in technology startups.  The fund, managed by Canbank Venture Capital Fund, is now in its divestment phase.

title: Guard's accidental gunshot kills man visiting bank in city
content: A customer was killed Tuesday after a security guard's gun discharged accidentally. Manish Kumar, a farmer, was updating his Aadhaar card at the Union Bank branch. The ex-serviceman guard, Vinod Kumar, was loading cartridges when the firearm discharged. The bullet struck Manish in the back, and he was rushed to the hospital. Police have arrested the guard and are investigating the incident further.

title: No ban on Jagannath movie, artists must enjoy creative liberty, says Supreme Court
content: The Supreme Court rejected a plea to ban an animated film on Mahaprabhu Jagannath.  Justices emphasized artists' creative expression and tolerance for depicting deities.  They noted that preventing such depictions would halt many religious television programs.  The court stated that the Censor Board's approval meant no judicial interference was needed.  It refused to restrict artistic creativity based on the objections of a few.

title: Jeff Bezos' quote on moving heavy, polluting industries to space and the future of travel
content: Sustainable tourism is essential for preserving Earth's natural beauty for future generations.  Healthy ecosystems are vital for the travel experiences that inspire millions of people.  Conscious travelers are increasingly choosing eco-friendly options and reducing waste.  Space technology offers practical ways to enhance travel safety and environmental management.  Protecting our planet ensures that Earth remains a beautiful destination for all.

title: 'Iran is going to get a beating': Trump threatens 'hard' response after attack on US base
content: United States President Donald Trump warned Iran of a forceful military response. American bases in Jordan faced missile attacks which the US intercepted. Iran's Revolutionary Guard claimed responsibility for the attempted surprise strike. US and Saudi forces also conducted overnight strikes against Iran-backed militias. Global markets reacted to the latest escalation in the Middle East.

title: Indian Embassy in US slams foreign media for misleading headline over PoK killings
content: The Indian Embassy criticized The New York Times for its inaccurate reporting.  The embassy stated Pakistan illegally occupies parts of Jammu and Kashmir.  Violent clashes have occurred in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir since early June.  Protests are ongoing over regional legislative assembly seats and alleged manipulation.  India attributes these protests to Pakistan's economic exploitation and oppression.

title: D4vd eligible for death penalty as prosecutors review Celeste Rivas murder case
content: Singer D4vd, David Anthony Burke, faces potential death penalty charges. Prosecutors are weighing the death penalty for the murder of Celeste Rivas Hernandez. Burke has pleaded not guilty to all serious charges against him. The case moves forward after a judge found sufficient evidence for trial. His next court hearing is scheduled for August 31 in Los Angeles.

title: Paredes faces 3 assault charges; FIFA charges Argentina over 'Malvinas' banner
content: FIFA initiated disciplinary proceedings against Argentina players and officials.  Charges include assault allegations and unsporting behaviour after the World Cup final.  The Argentine Football Association faces accusations for fan conduct and political demonstrations.  Players and staff may receive match suspensions and financial penalties for their actions.  FIFA will review all submissions before announcing its final verdict.

title: Why mosquitoes are choosing human blood more often, according to scientists
content: Scientists observed mosquitoes in Brazil's Atlantic Forest feeding on humans more often.  This shift suggests habitat loss is pushing mosquitoes towards human hosts.  DNA analysis revealed this surprising feeding pattern in protected forest areas.  Disappearing wildlife populations may force mosquitoes to seek new blood sources.  Protecting forests could help reduce future risks from mosquito-borne diseases.

title: Sanjeev Kumar predicted his early death, says Sachin Pilgaonkar on final days
content: Sachin Pilgaonkar recounted his missed final meeting with close friend Sanjeev Kumar.  He arrived at Sanjeev Kumar's residence later than planned that fateful afternoon.  Colleagues reflected on Sanjeev Kumar's demanding work and lifestyle choices.  His fascination with playing older characters stemmed from a palm reader's prediction.  Sanjeev Kumar passed away prematurely at the age of forty-seven.

title: J&K politicians urge UN, PM Modi to intervene over PoK killings
content: Political parties in Jammu and Kashmir are urging intervention over alleged killings. Over two dozen people were reportedly killed in firing by Pakistani security forces. National Conference president Farooq Abdullah called for a UN Human Rights Council team. CPM legislator MY Tarigami demanded an end to force and an inquiry. Unrest has escalated in PoK after authorities banned the Joint Awami Action Committee.

title: How Savannah James built a thriving business empire beyond LeBron James' fame
content: Savannah James has built a successful career through business, interior design, philanthropy, and community leadership. From launching furniture projects to mentoring young women and working with respected brands, she has created her own identity beyond basketball. While supporting her family, she has continued growing as an entrepreneur, proving that her achievements extend far beyond being LeBron James’ wife.

title: US Federal Reserve meet today: Kevin Warsh-led FOMC keeps interest rates unchanged
content: The US Federal Reserve, which began its two-day policy meeting on Tuesday, was widely expected to leave its benchmark interest rate unchanged.

title: Jammu and Kashmir: Schools closed in Kishtwar, Doda amid inclement weather
content: Authorities ordered school closures in Doda and Kishtwar districts due to inclement weather.  The Amarnath pilgrimage continued solely on the Baltal route with many devotees.  Vaishno Devi yatra also proceeded but only via the traditional Ardhkuwari track.  The Jammu-Srinagar national highway remained open for all vehicular traffic.  The IMD predicted continued rain and potential flash floods across the region.

title: Tourists no longer sleep in taxis, Farooq Abdullah hails hotel boom in Kashmir
content: In a recent statement, LG Manoj Sinha commended hotels for their role as facilitators of peace and their significant financial commitments to the sector. He pointed out that numerous hotels had overlooked crucial construction regulations. Farooq Abdullah highlighted the employment opportunities generated by hotels, reminiscing about a time when accommodation options were limited.

title: MP farmers breach barricades, reach within 1 km of CM Mohan Yadav's residence over moong MSP
content: Farmers in Bhopal protested over summer moong procurement at minimum support price. They breached police barricades and marched towards the Chief Minister's residence. The state government formed a committee to discuss issues with farmer representatives. Talks between the agriculture minister and farmer leaders concluded without a breakthrough. The protest continued with various demonstrations and roadside activities.

title: Watch: Terrifying one-punch knockout at CWG leaves boxer hanging through ropes
content: Orlando Holley-Sotomi of Wales delivered a powerful knockout during the Commonwealth Games boxing quarterfinal.  His opponent, Refiloe Thai, was sent through the ropes after a devastating right hand landed.  Medical staff quickly attended to the injured boxer, who thankfully showed signs of recovery.  This victory guarantees Holley-Sotomi at least a bronze medal in the competition.

title: Hyderabad: Trainee IPS officer arrested for sexual harassment of co-trainee
content: A trainee IPS officer was arrested for allegedly harassing a woman co-trainee. The accused faces charges of stalking and sexual harassment at the police academy. He reportedly sent abusive messages and made derogatory remarks to the complainant. The woman also alleged physical assault and blackmail attempts by the officer. Police registered a case under relevant sections of the law.

title: 'Like losing the woman of your life': Mancini apologises after dramatic Italy return
content: Roberto Mancini has apologised for his previous departure from the Italian national team. He admitted his exit was completely his fault and expressed deep regret. Mancini returns as Italy's coach after their World Cup qualification failures. He aims to restore the Azzurri to their former glory and win back trust. The team's new era begins with a UEFA Nations League match.

content: Suspense over the expansion of the Karnataka Cabinet continued on Wednesday, with the Congress high command once again deferring a final decision on the list of legislators to be inducted

content: The decision comes as nearly 2,000 farmers, who breached police barricades to reach the State capital, set up camp near Chief Minister Mohan Yadav’s residence

title: Dhanlaxmi Bank records ₹24.91 crore net profit in Q1 of FY 2026-27
content: Total business reached ₹35,190 crore as on June 30, 2026, from ₹29,051 crore as on June 30, 2025, recording 21.13 % growth.

title: Phase-I work on new bypass nears completion
content: The new stretch has been laid 3-4 km away from Singarapettai High Road to prevent heavy vehicles from entering Tirupattur town to reach other districts

title: Six persons held for illegal sand mining from irrigation tank, rivebed in Ranipet, Tirupattur
content: Initial inquiry revealed that special teams were formed in Ranipet to prevent illegal sand mining, smuggling of ganja and other banned substances

title: Kerala Police Association moves High Court against Home dept.’s order restructuring police forums
content: ACS (Home) ordered restructuring of KPA including all ranks from CPOs to grade SIs, and revamp of KPSOA by including ranks from SI to SP (non-IPS). The move renders another association, KPOA, redundant. KPA contends that each forum has its own objectives and questions the ACS authority to pass such an order

title: NHAI removes 361 encroachments from national highways after Supreme Court order
content: The nationwide drive ensured a ‘smooth and effective enforcement’ of removing illegal access points, encroachments, unauthorised structures and median cuts along highways, the NHAI said in a statement

title: Karnataka High Court questions conduct of Malur judicial officer on public road; stays FIR registered against three for overtaking her car
content: Taking serious exception to the conduct of a judicial officer on a public road, the High Court of Karnataka stayed the investigation against three persons based on a First Information Report registered against them for allegedly overtaking a private car of the judicial officer at Malur in Kolar district

content: Sambit Patra accuses the Congress leader of insulting students by dividing the protesters at Jantar Mantar into three categories — ‘students’, ‘idiots’ and ‘andhbhakt’ (blind devotees), and of repeatedly using the unparliamentary word ‘idiot’ in the Lok Sabha

content: Samyukta Kisan Morcha leader asks the Chief Minister to explain the underlying reason for the sudden reduction of the low-grade tobacco price to ₹110 per kg

title: 7 Killed In Helicopter Crash In Argentina: Officials
content: Seven people died when a firefighting helicopter in Argentina's western San Juan province crashed on Wednesday, a local official said.

title: Why Russia Is Seeking Telegram Founder Pavel Durov's Arrest
content: Russia announced on Wednesday that it was seeking the arrest of Telegram founder Pavel Durov over accusations of "complicity in terrorism", alleging he had let the platform be used for recruitment by Ukraine's security services.

title: Zelensky Says Massive Russian Airstrikes Overnight Likely On Ukraine
content: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky warned on Wednesday that Russia would likely carry out another massive attack on the country overnight, in a message posted on social media.

title: 5 Cops Killed, Dozens Injured In Terrorist Attack In Pakistan
content: Militants attacked a police post in northwestern Pakistan on Wednesday, triggering a gunbattle that killed five police officers and wounded about two dozen others, officials said.

title: After Row Over PM Modi's Video, Meta Writes To Centre, Outlines Safeguards
content: Outlining the enhanced safeguards for PM Modi's posts, Meta has said that prominent accounts to get additional oversight. Going forward, only senior Meta officials will vet such posts, sources said.

title: Trump, Netanyahu Explored All Iran Options Including Attack: Israeli Official
content: Netanyahu did not tell Trump that Israel's preference was for an attack on Iran, the official said in a briefing with reporters after the two men met in the White House on Tuesday.

content: A police official mentioned that the girl's family has consented to hand over the newborn to the Child Welfare Committee.

content: The accused IPS trainee officer earlier worked as a police constable and later joined IPS in 2025 after clearing the UPSC exam.

title: No Vada Pav, Samosa In And Near Maharashtra Schools: Food Body's Diktat
content: Foods high in fat, trans-fat, sugar and salt, commonly known as HFSS foods, can no longer be sold, given away or promoted within school premises or within a 50-metre radius of them.

content: Following the student's death, his family and villagers placed the body on the school premises and staged a protest, demanding action against the school authorities.

content: The company is most famous for developing the "Ovod" family of combat drones that the Russian army uses in its war with Ukraine.

content: The United States and Saudi Arabia said they had struck Iran-backed armed militants in Iraq in response to attacks on US forces and Saudi oil facilities.

content: In an update late Tuesday to a blog post detailing its probe into the incident, OpenAI said its AI agent affected these "publicly available services," though it did not name the companies.
